scenarios.action: Load each configured workspace, normalize execution defaults, and extract metadata.
scenarios.expected: Resolve repository roots, owners, targets, environments, versions, visibility, external relationships, and both concepts as specified by the behavior tables.

scenarios.action: Extract each configured Python and R API using the pinned static parsers.
scenarios.expected: Preserve the complete API rows and provenance; the baseline has four Rd location warnings and each focused case adds exactly its registered diagnostic.

scenarios.action: Parse all declared authored pages with their configured Panache profiles.
scenarios.expected: Match reviewed IR snapshots; the baseline has no parser diagnostics and each unsupported authored case has exactly one warning and a visible placeholder.

scenarios.action: Build both stateful pages with the declared Python and R kernels.
scenarios.expected: Preserve sequential state, ordered stdout/stderr, structured Markdown, local figures, and the allowed final error, matching the execution rows.

scenarios.action: Check and build each case separately; inspect outputs and attempted asset access.
scenarios.expected: Default-never and GFM source stay inert; generated Markdown cannot add executable cells; streams remain text; diagnostic codes, severities, and sources match the registry by command.

scenarios.action: Build both workspaces and inspect pages, links, source locations, concepts, navigation, and search.
scenarios.expected: All behavior-table URLs and targets resolve, search respects visibility and ecosystem ownership, concept labels distinguish equivalence from analogy, and all runtime assets are local.

scenarios.action: Run check, extract, generate, build, and serve with defaults where allowed, then from another directory with explicit --config, --input, --output, --host, and --port where supported.
scenarios.expected: Source commands default to ./diplodocus.toml; extract defaults to .diplodocus/documentation.sqlite beside that file, generate requires --input, site output defaults to ./site, and serve binds 127.0.0.1:8000. Explicit options take precedence; generate requires no source configuration.

scenarios.action: Run check for every case with kernels unavailable and no site or cache directory, then repeat with a preexisting cache.
scenarios.expected: Diagnostics match each check array; warnings exit zero and errors nonzero; no kernel discovery, runtime launch, network request, cache access/mutation, execution assets, snapshot publication, or site writes occur.

scenarios.action: Build each case in a fresh temporary workspace, then repeat error cases with an existing successful output tree.
scenarios.expected: Diagnostics match each build array; warnings succeed and remain visible, errors exit nonzero without a partial site or escaped asset, and a previous successful output is byte-identical after failure.

scenarios.action: Set every collection to mode = never in a temporary baseline; run extract from the configuration directory and another working directory, using default, relative, and absolute output paths with runtimes unavailable.
scenarios.expected: The default snapshot is .diplodocus/documentation.sqlite beside the configuration; an explicit --output is relative to the working directory or absolute. Every snapshot has the same canonical content, warnings remain visible, and no site or execution cache is created.

scenarios.action: Extract the temporary baseline and focused metadata and asset variants with every collection set to mode = never, copy only each database to an unrelated directory, delete the producing workspace, and load and query the copy read-only.
scenarios.expected: Recover both packages, semantic IDs, documents, references, concepts, checked-in images and downloads, presentation defaults, slugs, mounts, source links, diagnostics, and producer provenance. Asset bytes and canonical records match; no checkout paths, source reads, runtimes, caches, or SQLite sidecars are needed.

scenarios.action: Run extract with the baseline Python and R kernels enabled, copy only the completed database, delete sources, execution caches, and staged figures, and load the copy.
scenarios.expected: Recover all four executed pages, ordered structured outputs, execution provenance, two generated figures, and checked-in assets from the snapshot alone. Every asset fingerprint and byte count matches; extraction creates no site.

scenarios.action: Publish equivalent semantic data from relocated workspaces and different map insertion orders; change SQLite page layout and JSON object key order, then compare canonical exports and per-entity fingerprints.
scenarios.expected: Equivalent records and asset bytes have identical canonical exports and fingerprints despite different SQLite file bytes. Meaningful sequence order and binary bytes survive; editing one entity changes its fingerprint without changing unrelated entity fingerprints.

scenarios.action: Repeatedly extract the focused refresh workspace; edit retained items and pages, remove a package, target, collection, concept, relationship, and page, change assets and generated figures, disable execution, and repeat after manual database edits.
scenarios.expected: Retained entities keep their semantic IDs and receive current source content; deleted records, obsolete execution output, and unreferenced assets disappear while shared assets remain. Repeated refreshes are logically identical, manual edits and added tables are discarded, and no history or duplicate records accumulate.

scenarios.action: Load copies with independently unsupported storage, IR, and canonical encoding versions, including copies whose record tables cannot be decoded; also load a read-only valid database and a missing path.
scenarios.expected: Reject unsupported versions before decoding records, without migration or mutation. Loading a valid snapshot leaves its bytes and modification time unchanged; loading a missing path fails without creating a database or sidecars.

scenarios.action: Mutate isolated snapshots to remove required records or assets, corrupt JSON and asset bytes, alter fingerprints, introduce invalid identities, owners, paths, or dangling nested references, and forge invalid image contents; repeat structural mutations with recomputed fingerprints.
scenarios.expected: The loader rejects each malformed snapshot without changing its bytes or panicking. Valid fingerprints do not excuse invalid records, unsafe paths, dangling references, or invalid assets; supported external references remain valid without source files.

scenarios.action: Publish and replace complete snapshots while retaining an open reader; attempt publication with an active SQLite transaction, recovery sidecars, invalid records, and an occupied destination, then remove each obstruction and retry.
scenarios.expected: Readers see a complete old or new snapshot. Publication failures preserve the prior database, destination sentinels, and recovery files byte-for-byte, remove temporary storage, and permit a later refresh from current sources. Successful publication leaves one independently readable database without a journal or WAL dependency.

scenarios.action: After successful extraction, introduce invalid configuration, an unresolved source reference, an unavailable kernel, a disallowed cell error after a figure, an unresolved generated reference, and a publication obstruction in separate temporary attempts; repair the inputs and retry.
scenarios.expected: Each failed extract exits nonzero with its configuration, validation, execution, or publication error and preserves the previous snapshot bytes. No partial snapshot or earlier failed-cell figure is published, temporary storage is removed, and the repaired extraction publishes current content and assets.

scenarios.action: Request extract destinations overlapping configuration, package metadata, API sources, authored pages, local assets, declared environment inputs, input directories, or the execution cache, including symlink aliases and a download referenced only by generated Markdown.
scenarios.expected: Reject every overlapping destination without overwriting inputs. Known source conflicts fail before execution; generated-only asset conflicts fail after reference resolution but before publication. An explicitly linked snapshot download remains an input and cannot be replaced.

scenarios.action: Extract repeatedly into declared source trees using authored and API source extensions; add temporary storage, old-version snapshots, recovery sidecars, and in-boundary symlink aliases, then assemble, check, and revalidate the original input set.
scenarios.expected: Generated snapshots and storage never enter source discovery or declared-input fingerprints; repeated extraction has equal canonical content. Recovery files remain untouched, cross-boundary aliases still fail, and explicitly referenced database downloads remain inputs.

scenarios.action: In fresh workspace copies with identical declared environments, run extract followed by generate --input and compare with build; repeat with mode = never and with authorized deterministic execution. Copy only the database to a clean directory, remove sources and caches, disable runtimes, and generate twice with default and explicit output paths, recorded presentation defaults, and explicit presentation overrides.
scenarios.expected: Generation uses only the snapshot and generator, never reads workspace configuration or executes cells, and leaves input bytes unchanged. For matching presentation settings, separate stages and build have logically equal snapshots and identical site paths and bytes, including API pages, semantic links, concepts, search, and assets; repeated generation is identical.

scenarios.action: Run generate --input on missing, unsupported-version, malformed-record, dangling-reference, and corrupt-asset snapshots, first without a site and then with a successful site; try an output overlapping the input and stored HTML that violates the active sanitizer policy.
scenarios.expected: Generation validates before publication, rejects invalid inputs with a nonzero exit, and creates no partial site. The input database and prior site remain unchanged; stored HTML receives no trust from deserialization and only markup accepted by the active policy can render.

scenarios.action: Build and serve a successful site; fail extraction after changing sources, then allow extraction but introduce a route collision or site publication failure. Repair the fault and retry generation or a watched rebuild.
scenarios.expected: A failed extraction preserves the previous snapshot and site and never generates from stale records. A failed generation preserves the newly extracted snapshot and last successful site; retrying generation needs no extraction, and serve recovers on the same server.

scenarios.action: Start serve with an available loopback port and fetch the project landing page, one authored page, both API ecosystems, and an asset.
scenarios.expected: The initial build completes before serving; each expected route returns the generated bytes and shutdown releases the port and any kernel processes.

scenarios.action: Start serve, replace the page title with a unique marker in the temporary copy, and poll the page and search index with a bounded deadline.
scenarios.expected: The same server exposes the new title, navigation, and search entry without a restart.

scenarios.action: Start serve, add a TOML comment to pyproject.toml, then change DESCRIPTION Title; wait for each rebuild.
scenarios.expected: Each declared-environment change invalidates the corresponding execution cache and updates provenance while deterministic cell results remain stable.

scenarios.action: Start serve; change files in its output, execution cache, and an unrelated scratch directory while counting build events.
scenarios.expected: These changes do not schedule a rebuild; declared-input changes still do.

scenarios.action: Start from baseline, apply the unauthorized-execution overlay, wait for its diagnostic, remove it, and change a guide title.
scenarios.expected: The failed rebuild reports exactly the registered error and leaves every last-good output byte available; the subsequent valid change succeeds on the same server.

scenarios.action: Copy the workspace to two different absolute directories; build each with fresh caches, then rebuild from cache.
scenarios.expected: Compare every site path and byte and canonical snapshot records and asset contents, not SQLite file bytes; no checkout paths, temporary paths, timestamps, ports, or process IDs leak. Fresh and cached outputs have equal portable content under the cache contract.

scenarios.action: In disposable copies, add import-time Python and R load-hook traps; disable network access and run static checks and configured deterministic builds with tools preinstalled.
scenarios.expected: Documented package code is never imported, sourced, or loaded; no installer, fetch, or implicit network access occurs. Only authorized authored kernels run.

scenarios.action: Run formatting, linting, unit, golden, integration, link, and end-to-end checks in devenv and CI as their milestones land.
scenarios.expected: Every implemented fixture check passes without modifying checked-in inputs; all future behavior scenarios have a named milestone and none is counted as implemented by its specification alone.

scenarios.action: Copy the real configuration, its declared content, and environment input into a temporary workspace; parse every declared page.
scenarios.expected: The workspace has no API packages or targets; both profiles have reviewed IR, no parser diagnostics, and resolvable local source links and assets.

scenarios.action: Build and check the real project site, then preview with serve and edit a guide page.
scenarios.expected: Use the in-tree binary and the shared renderer; navigation, source links, search, local assets, and deterministic Python outputs are present, and the preview updates without another site generator.

scenarios.action: Build the real project docs in two distinct checkout directories with fresh caches; inspect both at / and /diplodocus/.
scenarios.expected: Output paths and bytes match; all internal links, fragments, assets, navigation, and search work at either hosting prefix without absolute local paths.

scenarios.action: In Milestone 10, exercise the docs workflow on a PR, main, a v* tag, and a manual dispatch.
scenarios.expected: PR and main builds validate only; v* tags and manual dispatches on main or v* tags deploy the validated Diplodocus output via github-pages with minimal Pages permissions. No other generator runs.

scenarios.action: From a clean checkout with declared tools installed, follow the checked-in instructions to check, build, and preview the acceptance site and the real project site, then extract a snapshot and generate the same site separately.
scenarios.expected: Both workflows reproduce the sites using the declared configuration and kernels for extraction and only the snapshot for generation; the guide explains explicit unsandboxed execution and requires no dependency installation or network access by Diplodocus.
